title: Asset size threshold and regulatory burden on bank profitability

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
The appropriate causal method for this analysis is a Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD). This is because we want to exploit the discontinuity at the $10B asset threshold to identify the causal effect of additional regulatory requirements on bank profitability. The key assumption is that, absent the treatment (crossing the threshold), banks just above and below the threshold (i.e., within a small bandwidth) are comparable in all respects except for the treatment.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(foreign)
library(rdrobust)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s28_data.csv")

# Select data near the cutoff
near_cutoff_data <- subset(data, near_cutoff == 1)

# Implement the RDD using running_var as the running variable and treated as the cutoff indicator
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = near_cutoff_data$y, x = near_cutoff_data$running_var, c = 0.5)

# Print the primary result (ATE at the cutoff)
summary(rdd_result)

# Basic robustness check: Re-estimate with different bandwidth
rd_robust_result2 <- rdrobust(y = near_cutoff_data$y, x = near_cutoff_data$running_var, c = 0.5, h = 0.2)

# Print the robustness check result
summary(rd_robust_result2)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect to find a negative effect on profitability (ROA) for banks whose asset size crosses the $10B threshold. This is because the additional regulatory requirements likely impose higher compliance costs and operational constraints, which might restrict profitability. The magnitude of this effect is uncertain without empirical analysis, but it is expected to be practically significant enough to motivate banks to manage their asset size strategically.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — asset threshold; test for bunching below $10B; local linear regression
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Banks just above threshold have lower ROA than just-below peers
